newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Bulk refined sugar ship seen shaking trade.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Bulk refined sugar ship seen shaking trade.

text.p: Delivery of the world's first purpose-built refined sugar bulk carrier vessel to Australia's Mackay Refined Sugars Pty Ltd signals a breakthrough for refined sugar as a traded commodity, company executives said on Tuesday.

The A$70 million MV MRS Pioneer, designed to carry 20,000 tonnes of refined sugar in bulk form, is only the third refined sugar bulk carrier in the world and signals a new direction in the efficient trade of refined sugar, they said.
"This represents a new market for Australian sugar," Neil Gregory, Mackay's marketing manager Australiasia, told Reuters during an inspection of the vessel.
Use of bulk refined sugar carriers such as the MRS Pioneer allow sugar refineries to be built next to sugar crushing mills in sugar growing districts, for bulk transport to final markets.
The sugar is usually automatically bagged on unloading.

Traditionally, the sugar trade has bulk-shipped raw sugar to refineries at ports, from where the final product is bagged and transported to final markets. The Pioneer provides major cost and efficiency savings, Mackay executives said.

Mackay Refined Sugars is a joint-venture between Mackay Sugar Co-operative and the global commodities and financial services conglomerate E.D. & F. Man, which owns or operates the world's other two refined sugar bulk carriers.

The bulk-in-bag-out (BIBO) method, used by Mackay since 1994 with the converted 20,000 tonne Innovator, which has now returned to the European route, has already helped Mackay into the growing Asian marketplace.
Mackay has captured about 100,000 tonnes a year of refined sugar exports to Asia, with about 60,000 a year sold to Indonesia, mainly to Coca-Cola Amatil Ltd's fast-growing bottling operations there.
As high-grade food products grew in developing Asia, so does demand for refined sugar.
The enormous potential in Asia for Mackay was limited mainly by its total refining capacity of about 350,000 tonnes a year, Gregory said.
Mackay also exports 50,000-60,000 tonnes of refined sugar a year to New Zealand.

Use of refined sugar BIBO carriers was causing a major restructuring of the industry and helping Mackay give Australia's long-established sugar refining group CSR Ltd a "run for its money", Gregory said.
Through the export trade, the BIBO vessel also protected Mackay to an extent from the ferocity of the current price war with CSR in Australia, Mackay executives said.

Mackay is presently engaged in legal action with CSR over fallout from unsuccessful merger moves three years ago and over price warfare in Australia and New Zealand. The case is scheduled to go before the High Court of Australia by April 18.
The Pioneer would be used by Mackay for delivery of refined sugar to distribution centres in Sydney, New Zealand, Indonesia, China, Sri Lanka and Iran, chief executive Jim Hughes said.
The Dutch-built Pioneer would enable Mackay to consolidate as one of the lowest-cost suppliers of refined sugar, he said.
Increased efficiencies in the company's operations would have a positive impact on its returns, which were currently affected by the price war, Hughes said.
As well as discharging in bulk at 500 tonnes an hour, the Pioneer can discharge in bags of varying sizes through its on-board bagging facility.
Built to Australian standards, the Pioneer flies the Australian flag and has a crew of 18 Australians.
It will be managed by BHP Ship Management.
